title: Fabrication of Magnetic Platforms for Micron-Scale Organization of Interconnected Neurons
protocol: Cut glass slides into 2 x 2 cm² using a scriber pen.
Clean the glass slides in acetone for 5 min in an ultrasonic bath.
Clean the glass slides in isopropanol for 5 min in an ultrasonic bath.
Dry the glass slides with ultra-high purity nitrogen gas.
Coat the glass with photoresist using spin-coating at 6,000 rpm for 60 s to attain a thickness of 1.5 μm.
Bake the coated glass at 100 °C for 60 s.
Expose the sample to light using an appropriate wavelength and photomask or mask-less lithography system.
Develop the exposed sample in a developer diluted in distilled water for 40 s according to manufacturer instructions.
Wash the developed sample in distilled water for 45 s.
Dry the sample with ultra-high purity nitrogen gas.
Inspect the pattern under an optical microscope.
Insert the sample into the main chamber of the deposition system and wait for base pressure (~5 × 10⁻⁸ Torr).
Open the gas flow, setting the argon flow rate to 28 sccm.
Ignite the sputter targets in the deposition system.
Set the sputter pressure to 3 mTorr.
Increase power on each target until a desired rate is achieved for Pd and Co80Fe20 layers.
Turn on rotation.
Deposit the FM multilayer, alternating between Co80Fe20 and Pd targets.
Open and close the target shutters for deposition.
Deposit 14 bilayers of Co80Fe20 (0.2 nm)/Pd (1.0 nm).
Finish with an additional 2 nm Pd capping layer.
Soak the sample in acetone for 30 min.
Rinse the sample with isopropanol.
Dry the sample with UHP nitrogen.
Attach the sample to the holder using double-sided tape.
Bond 4 wires to the sample, one on each leg of the cross electrode.
Set the sample-holder and sample inside the transport measurement system with a magnetic field perpendicular to the sample.
Perform VT measurements at room temperature.
Apply a current of 1 mA between contacts 1 and 3.
Measure the VT between contacts 2 and 4.
Apply a current between contacts 2 and 4.
Measure the voltage between contacts 1 and 3.
Calculate the difference between the voltages of both measurements.
Divide by 2 to obtain VT.
Sweep the magnetic field between 0.4 T and -0.4 T in steps of 5 mT for measurement.
Measure the transverse resistance (VT/I) as a function of the magnetic field.
Plot the transverse resistance vs. the magnetic field to determine the anomalous Hall signal.
Deposit the FM multilayer on the Si substrate.
Cut the sample into 6 squares of 4 x 4 mm2 size.
Stack the samples one on top of the other.
Arrange the stacked samples in the capsule perpendicular to the direction of the magnetic field.
Insert the capsule into the magnetometer and measure the magnetization at room temperature.
Sweep the magnetic field between -0.4 T and 0.4 T for measurement.
Calculate the total volume of the magnetic material.
Divide the magnetization by the total volume of the magnetic material to get magnetization per unit volume.
Plot the magnetization (per unit volume) vs. the magnetic field.
Subtract the diamagnetic background of the substrate from the high magnetic field response.
Extrapolate the saturation magnetization of the FM from the graph.
Insert a designated mass of MNPs into a synthetic polymer capsule.
Prepare 0.01 M HCl by adding 490 µL of HCl to 500 mL of autoclaved double-distilled water (DDW).
Dilute collagen type 1 in 0.01 M HCl at a ratio of 1:60-1:80 to obtain the final working concentration of 50 μg/mL.
Place 1.5 ml of diluted collagen solution in a 35 mm culture dish.
Leave the dish in the hood for 1 hour, covered.
Remove the collagen solution from the dish.
Wash the dish three times with sterile 1x phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Dilute collagen type 1 in 30% v/v ethanol at a ratio of 1:50.
For coating a 35 mm dish, add 20 μL of collagen to 1 mL of 30% ethanol.
Cover the dish with the solution and wait until all the solution evaporates, leaving the dish uncovered for a few hours.
Wash the glass slide three times with sterile 1x PBS.

Prepare basic growth medium for PC12 cell culture by adding 10% horse serum (HS), 5% fetal bovine serum (FBS), 1% L-glutamine, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 0.2% amphotericin to Roswell Park Medical Institute (RPMI) medium.
Filter the basic growth medium using a 0.22 µm nylon filter.
Prepare PC12 differentiation medium by adding 1% horse serum (HS), 1% L-glutamine, 1% penicillin/streptomycin, and 0.2% amphotericin to RPMI medium.
Filter the differentiation medium using a 0.22 µm nylon filter.
Grow cells in a non-treated culture flask with 10 mL of basic growth medium.
Add 10 mL of basic growth medium to the flask every 2-3 days.
Sub-culture the cells after 8 days.
Centrifuge the cell suspension in a centrifuge tube for 8 min at 200 × g and room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 3 mL of fresh basic growth medium.
Again, centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 200 × g and room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 3 mL of fresh differentiation medium.
Aspirate the cells 10x using a syringe and a needle to break up cell clusters.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Seed 10^6 cells in a regular uncoated 35 mm dish.
Add the calculated volume of MNP suspension and volume of differentiation medium to achieve the desired MNP concentration and total volume.
Mix the cells, MNPs, and differentiation medium.
Incubate the dish in a 5% CO2 humidified incubator at 37 °C for 24 h.
Centrifuge the cell suspension for 5 min at 200 × g at room temperature.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend the cells in 1 mL of fresh differentiation medium.
Count the cells using a hemocytometer.
Perform uptake protocol (section 5.1).
Seed 8 × 10^4 MNP-loaded cells on a 35 mm, collagen type I-coated dish in the presence of differentiation medium.
Add 1:100 fresh murine beta-nerve growth factor (β-NGF) after 24 h to achieve a final concentration of 50 ng/mL.
Renew the differentiation medium and add fresh murine β-NGF every 2 days.
Image the cells every 2 days using optical microscopy.
After network formation (6-8 days for PC12 cells), image the cells using confocal microscopy.
Observe the fluorescence of the particles.
Prepare the basic growth medium according to step 5.1.1.

Cultivate the PC12 cells with MNPs at different concentrations (0.1 mg/mL, 0.25 mg/mL, and 0.5 mg/mL in basic growth medium) and also without MNPs for the control in triplicate in a flat 96-well plate.
Incubate the cells for 24 h in a 5% CO2, humidified incubator at 37 °C.
Prepare blank wells containing medium without cells for background correction.
Thaw the XTT reagent solution and the reaction solution in a 37 °C bath immediately prior to use.
Swirl gently until clear solutions are obtained.
Mix 0.1 mL of activation solution with 5 mL of XTT reagent.
Add 50 µL of the reaction solution to each well.
Slightly shake the plate for an even distribution of the dye in the wells.
Incubate the plate in an incubator for 5 h.
Measure the absorbance of the sample against the blank wells using an ELISA reader at a wavelength of 450 nm.
Measure the reference absorbance using a wavelength of 630 nm and subtract it from the 450 nm measurement.
Subtract signal values from parallel samples of MNPs at the same tested concentrations as the cell samples.
Prepare basic growth medium according to step 5.1.1.
Cultivate PC12 cells with MNPs at different concentrations (0.1 mg/mL, 0.25 mg/mL, and 0.5 mg/mL in basic growth medium) and without MNPs as control in triplicate in a flat 96-well plate for 24 h.
Incubate the cells for 24 h in a 5% CO2 incubator at 37 °C.
Prepare blank wells containing medium without cells.
Wash the cells with 1x PBS.
Add resazurin-based reagent (10% w/v) to the medium and incubate for 2 h in a 37 °C incubator.
Place 150 µL aliquots of samples in the ELISA reader, and measure absorbance at an excitation wavelength of 560 nm and emission wavelength of 590 nm.
Subtract signal values from parallel samples of MNPs at the same tested concentrations as cell samples.
Lysate the cells by treating with 100 µL of 70% nitric acid for at least 15 min.
Add 5 mL of distilled deionized water (DDW) to the lysed cells.
Filter the solutions containing lysed cells.
Measure iron concentration using ICP.
Use cell count to record Fe concentration per cell.
Clean the patterned substrate with 70% ethanol.
Place the cleaned substrate in a 35 mm culture dish inside the hood.
Position a large magnet (~1500 Oe) below the patterned substrate for 1 min.
Remove the magnet by first lifting and moving the dish away from the magnet, then taking the magnet out of the hood.
Turn on the ultraviolet light for 15 min.
Coat the substrate with collagen type I according to section 4.2.
Suspend cells after cellular MNP uptake (section 5.1).
Seed 10^5 cells in a 35 mm culture dish and add 2 mL of differentiation medium.
Incubate the culture in a 5% CO₂, humidified incubator at 37 °C for 24 h.
Add fresh murine β-NGF (final concentration of 50 ng/mL) to the culture after 24 h.
Renew the differentiation medium and add fresh murine β-NGF every 2 days.
Image the cells every 2 days using light microscopy.
After network formation, perform immunostaining on the cells according to section 8.1.
Prepare a 4% paraformaldehyde solution by mixing 10 mL of 16% w/v PFA solution, 4 mL of 10x PBS, and 26 mL of DDW.
Prepare 50 mL of 1% PBT by adding 500 µL of a non-ionic surfactant to 50 mL of 1x PBS.
Prepare 50 mL of 0.5% PBT by mixing 25 mL of 1% PBT with 25 mL of 1x PBS.
Remove the supernatant medium from the cells.
Fix the MNP-loaded cells in 4% PFA for 15 min at room temperature inside a chemical hood.
Wash the MNP-loaded cells 3 times in 1x PBS, 5 min each wash, inside a chemical hood.
Permeabilize the MNP-loaded cells with 0.5% PBT for 10 min.
Incubate the MNP-loaded cells first in blocking solution for 45 min at room temperature and then with rabbit anti- α-tubulin antibody in blocking solution overnight at 4 °C.
Wash MNP-loaded cells 3 times in 1x PBS, 5 min each wash.
Incubate the MNP-loaded cells with Cy2-conjugated donkey anti-rabbit secondary antibody for 45 min in darkness and at room temperature.
Wash the MNP-loaded cells 3 times in 1x PBS, 5 min each wash.
Perform confocal imaging.
For tubulin, use an excitation wavelength of 492 nm and an emission wavelength of 510 nm.
For the MNPs (rhodamine), use an excitation wavelength of 578 nm and an emission wavelength of 613 nm.
Wash MNP-loaded cells 3 times in 1x PBS.
Incubate for 5 minutes between washes.
Remove excess liquid around the sample.
Add approximately 50 µL of mounting medium containing DAPI to cover a 22 mm x 22 mm area.
Incubate in darkness and at room temperature for 5 minutes.
Perform confocal imaging using an excitation wavelength of 358 nm and an emission wavelength of 461 nm for DAPI staining.
Use an excitation wavelength of 578 nm and an emission wavelength of 613 nm for MNPs (rhodamine).
Acquire phase images of cultured cells up to 3 days after treatment with NGF.
Open the acquired images in ImageJ, then use NeuronJ plug-in for semi-automatic neurite tracing and length measurement.
Convert traced data into binary images using NeuronJ's neurite tracer plugin.
Define the center of the soma in each cell image.
Perform Sholl analysis using NeuronJ plug-in to measure intersections at various distances from the cell body.
Repeat the experiment three times, analyzing more than 100 cells per experiment.
Acquire confocal microscopic images of cells with and without MNP uptake after 3 days of incubation.
Stain cells using DAPI (section 8.2).
Manually count cells atop or partially atop the pattern and those not touching it.
Repeat counting for three independent experiments.
Analyze more than 400 cells both with and without MNPs.
Calculate the relative proportion of cells atop magnetic patterns out of total cells, with and without MNPs.
Determine the percentage of effective magnetic pattern area by adding cell body diameter to pattern width.
Perform a single sample Z-test to determine if cell distribution is due to isotropic landing or preferential bias towards magnetic patterns.
Acquire confocal microscopic images of cells with and without MNP treatment after 8 days of incubation.
Stain cells using immuno-staining (section 8.1).
Measure the angle between the cell neurite and the magnetic stripes in both conditions using ImageJ software.
Analyze only neurites originating from somas located on magnetic stripes.
Plot the distribution of the neurites' angles relative to the direction of the stripes (Δθ).
Perform a Chi-squared test of the distribution of Δθ to demonstrate that the distribution is not normal or uniform.
